findings.description: Sharing the wrapper's statistics dictionary removes per-invocation isolation for concurrent and recursive calls. The async wrapper introduces the same regression.
findings.rationale: When two threads call the same decorated function, both retry copies now use the same dictionary despite having separate thread-local contexts. Starting the second call clears and resets the first call's statistics, and subsequent retries mix their counters, exposing incorrect statistics to callers. Likewise, overlapping async calls share their counters, and a recursive call overwrites the outer call's statistics.
